Subject: Legacy embed endpoint closeout — customer remediation & opt-in preservation

Team —

We need to lock in cross-functional asks for sunsetting the legacy embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings-legacy). Target deprecation date: 2027-06-30 (60 days from today). The high-level constraints: many customers rely on the legacy dimensionality and pre-processing semantics; we need to coordinate remediation, exceptions, and a short compatibility path for select enterprise customers.

Asks: 
- Sales/CS (Laura): identify customers who must be allowed an opt-in extension and confirm contractual implications (ACME is on the list). We need a golden list by EOD Monday.
- Engineering (Karthik): can infra support a lightweight compatibility shim (traffic-limited) for up to 90 days? If not, propose the shortest feasible window and rollback story.
- Product (Marissa): what are the evaluation gating criteria for leaving the legacy model variant online (safety / quality regressions)?
- Ops (Grace): support plan for telemetry, quota throttles, and a per-tenant fallback route.

Attachments: embed-migration-matrix.xlsx (work-in-progress), customer-notice-draft.md.

Risks to call out: customer regressions, unplanned latency increases if shim is high-overhead, and legal/finance implications for credits if migration is delayed.

Proposed immediate timeline: 
- 2027-05-03: cross-functional readiness sync + golden list 
- 2027-05-17: customer notices go out (CS-owned)
- 2027-06-30: endpoint fully disabled (subject to exemptions)

Please respond with blockers and confirm owners on the asks above.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Product Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Jordan / team —

Short answer: we can support a compatibility shim, but there are trade-offs. Notes:
- Shim design: translate legacy preprocessing and dimension mapping on the request path, then call the new model. That costs ~15-30ms additional latency per request and increases GPU memory at peak because we maintain a tiny mapping table per tenant.
- Throughput limits: we should gate the shim behind per-tenant rate limits (configurable, default 100 rps) to prevent tail latency issues.
- Duration: 60 days is straightforward operationally; 90 days is possible but increases exposure window for maintenance and drift.
- Rollback: we can implement fast-fail to the new model if CPU or memory is overloaded; but that risks returning incompatible vectors. We'd prefer a tenant-aware fallback that returns an explicit 409+help link.

Deliverables we need from Product: a clear compatibility contract (what exact inputs and preprocessing to emulate). From Sales: the authoritative golden list and start-of-extension timestamps.

I'll attach a short spec (compatibility-shim-spec.pdf) to the drive and follow up with a proposed infra checklist by EOD Monday.

Karthik
Head of Serving Infrastructure
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: compatibility-shim-spec.pdf

Subject: Re: Legacy embed endpoint closeout — customer remediation & opt-in preservation

Jordan —

Thanks for the outline. A couple of product/ML constraints to consider before we promise a long extension: 
- Model drift and quality parity: the legacy embeddings were produced by an earlier tokenizer and normalization. If we keep a compatibility shim that tries to emulate output, we must run parity evaluations for each tenant to ensure we don't silently degrade retrieval quality. That requires a sample prompt set (we should get that from CS) and ~2 weeks of evaluation.
- Canary plan: propose we offer a tenant-level canary for 2 weeks prior to full opt-in extension. During canary we collect relevance metrics and allow ACME to validate. 
- Resource amortization: maintaining the variant increases engineering and ops cost; product prefers 60-day support with an option for contractually defined paid extensions.

I'll prepare an evaluation checklist and a short sample set template. Also recommend adding a customer-facing migration FAQ to the draft notice.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Model Transitions
marissa_cole@redwood.com
